programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha Daolag-bhreac is Seillean ag ionnsachadh dè tha gabhail àite fon talamh – air leth inntinneach! Daolag-bhreac and Seillean are learning what happens underground - really interesting!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: It's early in the morning, and Isabelle and Oona are off to visit Otto before he goes to bed. Pip and Pop are already fast asleep, but they have taken up all the bedding. Oona, Isabelle and Otto split up to find soft, comfy things for Otto to sleep on. Seagull feathers are the hardest to get, but Isabelle is the best flier. She is sure she can do it, but her position as top flier is challenged by Otto. Tha e tràth sa mhadainn, 's tha Iseabail is Oona a' dèanamh air otto mus tèid e innte. Tha Pip is Pop mar tha nan suain, ach tha iad air còir a ghabhail air an stuth-leapa gu lèir.Sgaraidh Oona, Iseabail is Otto gus stuth cofhurtail is bog fhaighinn do dh'Otto 'son cadal air. Itean faoileig an rud 's dorr' a lorg, ach 's e Iseabail an t-itealaiche as fheàrr...tha i deimhinnt' gun tèid aic' air...ach tha a h-inbhe mar shàr-itealaiche ga dhùbhlanachadh le Otto.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Phoenix has picked up a strange, strong smell after playing with Mossy, and nobody knows where it came from. Phoenix needs a swim to wash it off, and on the way to the river, the friends try to figure out what caused the smell. They retrace Phoenix's steps, and discover lots of different smells in nature - but which one of them is the right match? Tha Phoenix air fàile làidir, neònach fhaighinn,'n dèidh bhith a' cluich còmh' ri Mosaidh, 's chan eil tuigs' aig duine cò às a dh'èirich e. Feumaidh Phoenix snàmh gus cùideas fhaighinn dheth, 's air an slighe chun na h-aibhne, tha na caraidean a' feuchainn ri thuigsinn dè dh'adhbhraich an samh.Gabhaidh 'ad gach ceum a ghabh Phoenix, a' fòghlam iomadh fàile nàdair eadar-dhealaichte...ach cò ac' a tha tighinn a-rèir fàileadh Phoenix?

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha Boban is Fuigheag taiceil do dhaolag-bhreac a tha na suain ach, aig a' cheann thall, tha iad ag ionnsachadh nach e peata a th’ innte Boban and Fuigheag are helpful to a sleeping ladybird today, but at the end of the day they learn that it’s not a pet.

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid a’ bèicearachd cuide ri a caraidean. An-diugh tha Beth agus Isaac cuide ri Linda agus iad a’ fuine cèic le cnò-chòco agus smeuragan. Ach mus tòisich iad, feumaidh iad dèanamh cinnteach gu bheil a h-uile cail tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, bidh iad a’ dèanamh liosta agus a’ dol dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach cò às a tha smeuragan a’ tighinn. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson a’ cheic a dhèanamh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd ga ithe! Linda Macleod and friends cook a number of tasty dishes. She is joined by Beth and Isaac to bake a delicious coconut and blackberry cake. However, before they start, they must be sure they have all the ingredients. If not, they make a list and go shopping. Linda and her friends also find out more about how blackberries are grown, and then it's back into the kitchen to bake the cake before sitting down at the table to taste it.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Ailig Dòmhnallach a’ leughadh Eanraig agus an Yeti. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Russell Ayto agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Alec MacDonald reads Eanraig agus an Yeti, written by Russell Ayto and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair tha picnic rìoghail dol a ghabhail àite sa phàirc, tha Stella air a dearg nàrachadh, gun fhios nach fhaic a caraidean i an sin. Stella is really embarrassed in case friends see her when she is with her family at a royal picnic in the park.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair tha Partaidh nam Fiaclairean dol a thachairt, the Mrs Oh 'g iarraidh buidealair. Ach chan eil Mgr P deònach taic a thoirt seachad. Dè nì Stella is an Teaghlach Rìoghail airson cuideachadh leis a’ chuirm? When the Dentist Party is about to take place, Mrs Oh would like a butler. But Mr P isn’t prepared to help out. What will Stella and the Royal Family do to help at the event?

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Gun teagamh sam bith, tha cùisean doirbh nuair a tha teas is mòr-thiormachd ann is an staing gann de dh'uisg’. Tha sin a' fàgail na Gumbalan feumach air dìon bho na Bògaisean. Things are difficult when the heat and drought lasts for so long that the moat is empty of water. It leaves Gumbalan in need of protection from Bògaisean.

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Tha creutair mì-àbhaisteach anns an uisge – a’ coiseachd air grunnd na mara agus a’ tarraing buaireadh. Dè idir a th’ ann? Feumar a stad – ach ciamar? There’s an unusual creature in the water, walking across the ocean floor and causing havoc. What on earth is it? It must be stopped, but how?

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Serie A
programme.desc: Serie A - Napoli v Bologna Ball-coise beò bho Serie A le Napoli a’ cur fàilte air Bologna bho pàirce Diego Armando Maradona. Aithris bho Derek MacAoidh. Join BBC Alba for live Serie A football action as Napoli host Bologna at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. Commentary comes from Derek Mackay.

programme.title: Alba fon Talamh/Scotland Underground
programme.desc: In the Highlands and Islands, Calum explores the caves of Assynt, a Unesco global geopark, before travelling north to Orkney where there is a wealth of archeological underground sites. But it is also an example of the modern use of subterranean sites: oil to service the Scapa Flow naval sites was hidden underground in vast tanks beneath Wee Fea hill. The war theme continues as Calum visits a Cold War underground bunker in Inverness. Anns a’ Ghàidhealtachd agus na h-Eileanan, bheir Calum cuairt tro uamhan Asainte, geò-pàirc cruinneil UNESCO. À sin, thèid e tuath gu Arcaibh far a bheil beartas de làraich arceòlach fon talamh, ach cuideachd eisimpleir nas ùire den fho-thalamh a chleachdadh. Fo chnoc Wee Fea, tha na tancaichean mòra a bha a’ cumail ola ri làrach a’ Chabhlaich Rìoghail ann an Scapa Flow. A’ cumail ri tèama a’ chogaidh, ann an Inbhirnis tadhlaidh Calum air buncair bho àm a’ Chogaidh Fhuair. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: The community gathers for a fundraiser ceilidh for Old Mary who is recovering from her mill accident. A drunken Boyd confronts Mairead and Cairistiona in front of everyone at the ceilidh. Things turn sour between Johan and Murdina resulting in a mysterious fire starting at the hotel, trapping Murdina and Boyd inside. Will they make it out alive? Tha a’ choimhearsnachd a’ cruinneachadh aig cèilidh gus airgead a thogail do Mhàiri, a tha fhathast a’ faighinn seachad air an tubaist aice ‘sa mhuileann. Tha smùid air Boyd ‘s e a’ cur aghaidh air Mairead ‘s Cairistiona air beulaibh a h-uile duine aig a’ chèilidh. Tha cùisean a’ dol ceàrr eadar Johan is Murdina, a’ fàgail gu bheil teine a’ tòiseachadh anns an taigh-òsta – le Murdina agus Boyd glaiste na bhroinn. Am faigh iad às beò? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Lost Cities of the Ancients
programme.desc: It was one of the greatest vanishing acts in history. More than 3,000 years ago a mysterious and ruthless civilisation rose from nothing, created a brutal and unstoppable army and built an empire that rivalled Egypt and Babylon. Yet, just as it was at the height of its powers, the great empire suddenly vanished from history. This is the story of the formidable Hittites, a civilisation bent on world domination. Their long-lost capital, Hattusha, which disappeared thousands of years ago, was recently rediscovered. Archaeologists have unearthed one of the most astonishing and ingenious cities of the ancient world, featuring rings of impenetrable walls, secret tunnels, temples, palaces and a vast pyramid-like structure facing Egypt. Buried in this lost city is one of the greatest libraries of the ancient world. All the secrets of the mysterious Hittite empire were written in two codes - one a unique form of hieroglyphs. Using these deciphered texts, the film recreates the ancient world of the Hittites, telling the story of what happened to them, and what caused an empire built to last forever to vanish so completely from history.

programme.title: Art of Scandinavia
programme.desc: Scandinavia - a land of extremes, on the edge of Europe. Andrew Graham-Dixon explores the extraordinary art to come out of the dark Norwegian soul, most famous for producing The Scream by Edvard Munch.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: The team explore the remarkable story of Jodrell Bank Observatory and its towering Lovell Telescope, which scientists have used to listen to the cosmos for almost 70 years.

programme.title: British Art at War: Bomberg, Sickert and Nash
programme.desc: In the years preceding 1914, David Bomberg, Walter Sickert and Paul Nash set out to paint a new world, but, as the century unfolded, found themselves working in the rubble. David Bomberg is now recognised as the most startlingly original British painter of his generation, but died in obscurity more than half a century ago. A Jewish immigrant from London's east end, his early modernist works pushed art to its limits. Fighting at the Somme, David Bomberg watched the world splinter and fall apart just like the works of art he had created. Bomberg spent the rest of his life searching for order in an increasingly disordered world, and his wanderings took him as far as Palestine, before he settled at the end of his life in Ronda, Spain. When he died in 1957, embattled and in poverty, he seemed to be no more than a footnote in the history of British art. However, the works that survive David Bomberg tell their own story. Combative and iconoclastic, he remains the most elusively original British painter of the 20th century.

programme.title: Art That Made Us
programme.desc: With the industrial revolution transforming the British Isles, the cities and country are divided, and artists respond to the upheavals to lives and the landscape.

programme.title: An Art Lovers' Guide
programme.desc: In the first of a series of city adventures, Janina Ramirez and Alastair Sooke head to Lisbon, rapidly becoming one of Europe’s most popular tourist destinations. Winding through the city’s cobbled streets, from its steep hills to the picturesque shore line, the cultural riches they encounter reveal the city's fascinating history. From a spectacular monument to the maritime globetrotting of Portugal’s golden age and the work of a photographer documenting the city's large African population, they discover a complex history of former glories and a darker, slave-trading past. Their journey also uncovers the impact of 20th-century dictatorship on the city's artistic and cultural life, through the work of contemporary artists Paula Rego and Joana Vasconcelos. And they discover how the city's location on the west coast of Europe, looking out to the Atlantic, has shaped the cosmopolitan spirit of the city. In one of the city's Fado clubs, Alastair and Nina enjoy the popular Portuguese folk music, whose beautiful melodies celebrate a yearning for home, once sung by sailors dreaming of their return.

Winding through the city’s cobbled streets, from its steep hills to the picturesque shore line, the cultural riches they encounter reveal the city's fascinating history. From a spectacular monument to the maritime globetrotting of Portugal’s golden age and the work of a photographer documenting the city's large African population, they discover a complex history of former glories and a darker, slave-trading past. Their journey also uncovers the impact of 20th-century dictatorship on the city's artistic and cultural life, through the work of contemporary artists Paula Rego and Joana Vasconcelos. And they discover how the city's location on the west coast of Europe, looking out to the Atlantic, has shaped the cosmopolitan spirit of the city. In one of the city's Fado clubs, Alastair and Nina enjoy the popular Portuguese folk music, whose beautiful melodies celebrate a yearning for home, once sung by sailors dreaming of their return.

programme.title: What Happened at...?
programme.desc: The 1986 explosion at Chernobyl triggered a public health emergency across Europe. Today, the site's strategic location continues to be a flashpoint in Russia's war with Ukraine. Forty years on from the disaster, Jordan Dunbar travels to Chernobyl to examine the events that led to the world's worst nuclear accident and what we can learn from them today.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav and Nick listen in to a highly skilled scammer, posing as a broadband provider, who claims to fix issues that you might have with your internet connection. This slick scammer takes full control of a man’s phone and computer. With the victim completely under his influence, and the ground interceptors over an hour away, the team must try everything they can to disrupt the scam and reach the man before he pays out. Interceptor Mark also takes a deep-dive investigation into the world of sextortion scammers – fraudsters who blackmail their victims by threatening to release intimate pictures and videos.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman helps ex-England international and football hard man Neil ‘Razor’ Ruddock find his softer side as he and his wife Leah escape to the country in rural Kent. Razor’s tough-guy persona is put to the test when a 15th-century thatched cottage causes him concern about spiders, but the former pro shows that he is still as sharp as ever in a house hunt full of wit and warmth.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Bristol-based Diana and her daughter Millie are dreaming of a fresh start in the sunny Somerset countryside, with enough land for a little flower farm to bloom. Alistair Appleton is on hand to help them sow the seeds of their new life. Along the way, he meets a couple who have swapped cider apples for grape vines, planting their very own vineyard in the heart of this amazing county.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where four contestants – in this episode, basketball team Terry, Charlie, Meg and Kathy – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Rav and Nick listen in to a highly skilled scammer, posing as a broadband provider, who claims to fix issues that you might have with your internet connection. Interceptor Mark also takes a deep-dive investigation into the world of sextortion scammers – fraudsters who blackmail their victims by threatening to release intimate pictures and videos.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where four contestants – in this episode, basketball team Terry, Charlie, Meg and Kathy – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav and Nick listen in to a highly skilled scammer, posing as a broadband provider, who claims to fix issues that you might have with your internet connection. This slick scammer takes full control of a man’s phone and computer. With the victim completely under his influence, and the ground interceptors over an hour away, the team must try everything they can to disrupt the scam and reach the man before he pays out. Interceptor Mark also takes a deep-dive investigation into the world of sextortion scammers – fraudsters who blackmail their victims by threatening to release intimate pictures and videos.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman helps ex-England international and football hard man Neil ‘Razor’ Ruddock find his softer side as he and his wife Leah escape to the country in rural Kent. Razor’s tough-guy persona is put to the test when a 15th-century thatched cottage causes him concern about spiders, but the former pro shows that he is still as sharp as ever in a house hunt full of wit and warmth.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Bristol-based Diana and her daughter Millie are dreaming of a fresh start in the sunny Somerset countryside, with enough land for a little flower farm to bloom. Alistair Appleton is on hand to help them sow the seeds of their new life. Along the way, he meets a couple who have swapped cider apples for grape vines, planting their very own vineyard in the heart of this amazing county.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where four contestants – in this episode, basketball team Terry, Charlie, Meg and Kathy – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: On patrol in Belfast, Perri and Adam respond to reports of cars performing dangerous stunts on the streets while large crowds look on. When they arrive, the cars scatter and the Peelers don’t catch anyone. Later, they put in place an operation to disrupt a group of so-called differs – drivers who dangerously and illegally spin their cars in circles on main roads. The Peelers call in air support and try to catch a differ in the act. Back in Belfast, the team receive reports of two women being disruptive at a hotel. programme.title: Scam Interceptors

Interceptor Mark also takes a deep-dive investigation into the world of sextortion scammers – fraudsters who blackmail their victims by threatening to release intimate pictures and videos.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman helps ex-England international and football hard man Neil ‘Razor’ Ruddock find his softer side as he and his wife Leah escape to the country in rural Kent. Razor’s tough-guy persona is put to the test when a 15th-century thatched cottage causes him concern about spiders, but the former pro shows that he is still as sharp as ever in a house hunt full of wit and warmth.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Bristol-based Diana and her daughter Millie are dreaming of a fresh start in the sunny Somerset countryside, with enough land for a little flower farm to bloom. Alistair Appleton is on hand to help them sow the seeds of their new life. Along the way, he meets a couple who have swapped cider apples for grape vines, planting their very own vineyard in the heart of this amazing county.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where four contestants – in this episode, basketball team Terry, Charlie, Meg and Kathy – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav and Nick listen in to a highly skilled scammer, posing as a broadband provider, who claims to fix issues that you might have with your internet connection. This slick scammer takes full control of a man’s phone and computer. With the victim completely under his influence, and the ground interceptors over an hour away, the team must try everything they can to disrupt the scam and reach the man before he pays out. Interceptor Mark also takes a deep-dive investigation into the world of sextortion scammers – fraudsters who blackmail their victims by threatening to release intimate pictures and videos.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman helps ex-England international and football hard man Neil ‘Razor’ Ruddock find his softer side as he and his wife Leah escape to the country in rural Kent. Razor’s tough-guy persona is put to the test when a 15th-century thatched cottage causes him concern about spiders, but the former pro shows that he is still as sharp as ever in a house hunt full of wit and warmth.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Bristol-based Diana and her daughter Millie are dreaming of a fresh start in the sunny Somerset countryside, with enough land for a little flower farm to bloom. Alistair Appleton is on hand to help them sow the seeds of their new life. Along the way, he meets a couple who have swapped cider apples for grape vines, planting their very own vineyard in the heart of this amazing county.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where four contestants – in this episode, basketball team Terry, Charlie, Meg and Kathy – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

With the victim completely under his influence, and the ground interceptors over an hour away, the team must try everything they can to disrupt the scam and reach the man before he pays out. Interceptor Mark also takes a deep-dive investigation into the world of sextortion scammers – fraudsters who blackmail their victims by threatening to release intimate pictures and videos.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman helps ex-England international and football hard man Neil ‘Razor’ Ruddock find his softer side as he and his wife Leah escape to the country in rural Kent. Razor’s tough-guy persona is put to the test when a 15th-century thatched cottage causes him concern about spiders, but the former pro shows that he is still as sharp as ever in a house hunt full of wit and warmth.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Bristol-based Diana and her daughter Millie are dreaming of a fresh start in the sunny Somerset countryside, with enough land for a little flower farm to bloom. Alistair Appleton is on hand to help them sow the seeds of their new life. Along the way, he meets a couple who have swapped cider apples for grape vines, planting their very own vineyard in the heart of this amazing county.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where four contestants – in this episode, basketball team Terry, Charlie, Meg and Kathy – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav and Nick listen in to a highly skilled scammer, posing as a broadband provider, who claims to fix issues that you might have with your internet connection. This slick scammer takes full control of a man’s phone and computer. With the victim completely under his influence, and the ground interceptors over an hour away, the team must try everything they can to disrupt the scam and reach the man before he pays out. Interceptor Mark also takes a deep-dive investigation into the world of sextortion scammers – fraudsters who blackmail their victims by threatening to release intimate pictures and videos.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman helps ex-England international and football hard man Neil ‘Razor’ Ruddock find his softer side as he and his wife Leah escape to the country in rural Kent. Razor’s tough-guy persona is put to the test when a 15th-century thatched cottage causes him concern about spiders, but the former pro shows that he is still as sharp as ever in a house hunt full of wit and warmth.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Bristol-based Diana and her daughter Millie are dreaming of a fresh start in the sunny Somerset countryside, with enough land for a little flower farm to bloom. Alistair Appleton is on hand to help them sow the seeds of their new life. Along the way, he meets a couple who have swapped cider apples for grape vines, planting their very own vineyard in the heart of this amazing county.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate how a firm providing equipment to children with special educational needs has let down dozens of families and charged unlawful fees. Also on the programme, the retiree who sent her second-hand car back to the dealership for repairs but instead received a call from police saying it had been found vandalised. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help a woman who received a parking ticket while on holiday, despite leaving her vehicle in the care of an airport parking firm.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer

programme.desc: Railway Wood is a replica trench in a Kent woodland based on a First World War trench in Belgium. David Harper walks the duckboards with a historian who helped to create it.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav and Nick listen in to a highly skilled scammer, posing as a broadband provider, who claims to fix issues that you might have with your internet connection. This slick scammer takes full control of a man’s phone and computer. With the victim completely under his influence, and the ground interceptors over an hour away, the team must try everything they can to disrupt the scam and reach the man before he pays out. Interceptor Mark also takes a deep-dive investigation into the world of sextortion scammers – fraudsters who blackmail their victims by threatening to release intimate pictures and videos.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman helps ex-England international and football hard man Neil ‘Razor’ Ruddock find his softer side as he and his wife Leah escape to the country in rural Kent. Razor’s tough-guy persona is put to the test when a 15th-century thatched cottage causes him concern about spiders, but the former pro shows that he is still as sharp as ever in a house hunt full of wit and warmth.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Bristol-based Diana and her daughter Millie are dreaming of a fresh start in the sunny Somerset countryside, with enough land for a little flower farm to bloom. Alistair Appleton is on hand to help them sow the seeds of their new life. Along the way, he meets a couple who have swapped cider apples for grape vines, planting their very own vineyard in the heart of this amazing county.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where four contestants – in this episode, basketball team Terry, Charlie, Meg and Kathy – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

With the victim completely under his influence, and the ground interceptors over an hour away, the team must try everything they can to disrupt the scam and reach the man before he pays out. Interceptor Mark also takes a deep-dive investigation into the world of sextortion scammers – fraudsters who blackmail their victims by threatening to release intimate pictures and videos.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman helps ex-England international and football hard man Neil ‘Razor’ Ruddock find his softer side as he and his wife Leah escape to the country in rural Kent. Razor’s tough-guy persona is put to the test when a 15th-century thatched cottage causes him concern about spiders, but the former pro shows that he is still as sharp as ever in a house hunt full of wit and warmth.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Bristol-based Diana and her daughter Millie are dreaming of a fresh start in the sunny Somerset countryside, with enough land for a little flower farm to bloom. Alistair Appleton is on hand to help them sow the seeds of their new life. Along the way, he meets a couple who have swapped cider apples for grape vines, planting their very own vineyard in the heart of this amazing county.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where four contestants – in this episode, basketball team Terry, Charlie, Meg and Kathy – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: The Harbour
programme.desc: Aberdeen Harbour on the north east coast of Scotland, is one of Britain's oldest businesses and one of Europe's most modern ports. It is the heartbeat of the offshore oil and gas industry. Every year, more than eight thousand boats pass through the harbour waters, helped by the hidden world of the men and women who keep it running 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. This is their story. In this first programme of the series, the Harbour's best known barmaid, Val Morrison of the Crown & Anchor, is getting ready for a Halloween party in the pub. We meet the Harbour boatmen, a small close knit team of men who between them must ensure every boat is safely docked. And we're aboard the massive Bibby Sapphire as she heads out to sea, where saturation diver Terry Dearlove faces a tricky pipeline installation. When you're working 185 metres beneath the waves and living in a tiny pressurised chamber, it's the little things that mean a lot.

programme.title: The Harbour
programme.desc: Aberdeen Harbour on the north east coast of Scotland, is one of Britain's oldest businesses and one of Europe's most modern ports. It is the heartbeat of the offshore oil and gas industry. Every year, more than eight thousand boats pass through the harbour waters, helped by the hidden world of the men and women who keep it running 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. This is their story. In this episode: It's very rare to see the harbour closed, but abnormally high winds mean it's just too dangerous to stay open. Everything has to stop, but the delays cost thousands. Boatmen Alan Cowper takes his daughter to try out for Scotland's under-15 football team but faces an excruciating wait to hear whether she gets in. VTS controller Ralph Greig has decided a change of career is required, while out at sea on the Bibby Sapphire, saturation diver Terry Dearlove begins the lengthy process of decompression. With a North Sea storm looming, will he get back to Aberdeen in time to get home for his daughter's 18th birthday?

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Beth and Eric think Ian is taking them out for their 30th wedding anniversary dinner but find instead that he and Gordon have organised a surprise party at their house. And the gang is all there. What more could you ask from a party? The buffet table is groaning with food, the champagne is flowing and Christine has brought a homemade trifle as a present. There is a wander down memory lane, a look at the Bairds' wedding album and an illuminating quiz. Ian tries to keep the focus on the anniversary couple but a drunken Cathy tries to prompt wedding proposals from reluctant boyfriends Ian and Alan, and treats Eric, Beth and the rest of the guests to a replay of her and Colin's first wedding dance.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie, Arlene and Shahbaz head to the Isle of Bute, the jewel of the Firth of Clyde. Dougie meets island dairy farmers staying resilient as another milk pricing crisis looms. He also visits the grounds of Mount Stuart House to delve into one of Bute’s biggest wildlife mysteries. Arlene joins a 'superhero' beach ranger at Scalpsie Bay to uncover what is washing up on Bute’s shores. She also discovers how preschool children are getting their first taste of farming life. And Shahbaz meets a Syrian family who fled war and have built a new life on the island, finding welcome and opportunity there.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Planting borders and planning for cut flowers are on Lizzie Schofield and Brian Cunningham’s to-do list at the garden. Lizzie is direct sowing in the new cuttings area and Brian is in the zig-zag border, planting varieties that will grow tall, making them ideal for the back of a plot without requiring support or staking. Brian kicks off this year’s collection of plants being cultivated in the 6x8ft glasshouse. This is the most common-sized domestic greenhouse, so if you are lucky enough to have one, Brian has some great ideas for this season. Lizzie is the first of the presenters to start work in her competition plot. The theme this year is planting that will appeal to one of the senses, and Lizzie has one of the most challenging: touch. Plus, there is a report on the alpine collection at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, and all the usual handy hints.

programme.title: Charlie Cooper’s Myth Country
programme.desc: Charlie Cooper’s odyssey takes him to Wiltshire, home to ancient sites such as Stonehenge, Avebury and the Westbury chalk horse. He wants to get to the bottom of why humans feel the need to leave marks on the landscape. He soon turns his investigation towards a far more recent phenomenon, crop circles, hoping to settle a debate that has plagued his family for years. They believe that crop circles are the work of aliens, but Charlie strongly doubts that. He meets with farmers and secretive 'croppies' (humans who create crop circles), trying to find out how these vast and intricate shapes appear overnight. Helped by his friend Scott, Charlie takes his research one step further and attempts to shed light on the phenomenon by making his very own crop circle. The humorous trip aboard an old AA van shows him that you only need to scratch the surface anywhere in this land to discover that folklore, myth and legend are very much alive and exert a beguiling power.

programme.title: Charlie Cooper’s Myth Country
programme.desc: Charlie Cooper has always loved the stories of King Arthur, especially the ones about his buried treasures. He digs out his metal detector, says goodbye to his family and embarks on an Arthurian investigation. He travels to Wales, the land of dragons and song, on a mission to discover if King Arthur was a real man or just a myth and if there’s any truth behind this treasure story. In the process, he meets treasure hunters of different sorts, a recorder of rare and ancient folk songs, and finds what he refers to as 'his tribe', a metal-detecting club from South Wales. He’s optimistic he will return home a rich man - if not in wealth, then certainly in knowledge.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: A Dalek fleet surrounds a lone rebel ship, and only the Doctor can help it now. With the Doctor facing his greatest enemy, he needs Clara by his side. Confronted with a decision that could change the Daleks forever, he is forced to examine his conscience and ask himself whether he is truly a good man.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: In a sun-dappled Sherwood Forest, the Doctor discovers an evil plan from beyond the stars and strikes up an unlikely alliance with Robin Hood. With all of Nottingham at stake, the Doctor must decide who is real and who is fake. Can impossible heroes actually exist?

programme.title: Sin City: The Real Las Vegas
programme.desc: Tir Dhondy reveals the realities behind modern Las Vegas. She goes to a high-octane pool party to discover how casinos are cashing in on the party scene.

programme.title: Sin City: The Real Las Vegas
programme.desc: Tir goes even further into the underbelly of Las Vegas to investigate how the reinvention of the city to pull in a new generation of visitors is affecting those who live and work there.

programme.title: Charlie Cooper’s Myth Country
programme.desc: Charlie Cooper’s odyssey takes him to Wiltshire, home to ancient sites such as Stonehenge, Avebury and the Westbury chalk horse. He wants to get to the bottom of why humans feel the need to leave marks on the landscape. He soon turns his investigation towards a far more recent phenomenon, crop circles, hoping to settle a debate that has plagued his family for years. They believe that crop circles are the work of aliens, but Charlie strongly doubts that. He meets with farmers and secretive 'croppies' (humans who create crop circles), trying to find out how these vast and intricate shapes appear overnight. Helped by his friend Scott, Charlie takes his research one step further and attempts to shed light on the phenomenon by making his very own crop circle. The humorous trip aboard an old AA van shows him that you only need to scratch the surface anywhere in this land to discover that folklore, myth and legend are very much alive and exert a beguiling power.

programme.title: Charlie Cooper’s Myth Country
programme.desc: Charlie Cooper has always loved the stories of King Arthur, especially the ones about his buried treasures. He digs out his metal detector, says goodbye to his family and embarks on an Arthurian investigation. He travels to Wales, the land of dragons and song, on a mission to discover if King Arthur was a real man or just a myth and if there’s any truth behind this treasure story. In the process, he meets treasure hunters of different sorts, a recorder of rare and ancient folk songs, and finds what he refers to as 'his tribe', a metal-detecting club from South Wales. He’s optimistic he will return home a rich man - if not in wealth, then certainly in knowledge.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: A Dalek fleet surrounds a lone rebel ship, and only the Doctor can help it now. With the Doctor facing his greatest enemy, he needs Clara by his side. Confronted with a decision that could change the Daleks forever, he is forced to examine his conscience and ask himself whether he is truly a good man.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: In a sun-dappled Sherwood Forest, the Doctor discovers an evil plan from beyond the stars and strikes up an unlikely alliance with Robin Hood. With all of Nottingham at stake, the Doctor must decide who is real and who is fake. Can impossible heroes actually exist?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the final leg of his journey, Michael travels to South Korea’s south west, where food, protest and landscape reveal the values that have shaped the modern nation. Arriving by high-speed train in Gwangju, he explores the region’s deep-rooted food culture, meeting a prizewinning kimchi maker to learn how Korea’s iconic fermented dish has sustained communities for centuries and become a symbol of shared labour and tradition. Michael then confronts a darker chapter in South Korea’s history at the May 18th Memorial Park, where a survivor of the 1980 Gwangju Uprising recounts how student-led protests against military rule were brutally suppressed and why the events are now regarded as the cornerstone of Korean democracy. Leaving the mainland, Michael crosses by ferry to Jeju Island, a volcanic landscape dominated by Mount Halla. Exploring lava tubes with a volcanologist, he uncovers how the island was formed before meeting the Haenyeo, Jeju’s legendary female free divers.

programme.title: Secret Garden
programme.desc: David Attenborough reveals how a remote garden on Scotland’s west coast has become an oasis for barn owls and pine martens as they battle the elements to feed, breed and survive.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Kelly Cates presents highlights from the day’s four Premier League games including West Ham against Arsenal, a game that could have huge implications at the bottom of the table and in the title race. With European places at stake, Aston Villa travel to relegated Burnley, and Everton are at Crystal Palace, while Nottingham Forest look to move clear of the relegation zone at home to Newcastle.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Celebrating the programme's 50th year, Clive Myrie presents the first heat of this series of the classic quiz where contenders face the famous black chair with the ultimate goal of becoming the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are Francisco de Goya, Peaky Blinders, Team GB at the 2020 Summer Olympics and the Philip Marlowe novels of Raymond Chandler.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions while our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The Clean It Fix It team is in West London to help the Parkinson family. With four young children, their house is overrun with toys, the hallway is a dumping ground, and the kitchen is in desperate need of a clean. The team has just one day to transform the space into a clean and clutter-free family home.

programme.title: Big Cats 24/7
programme.desc: The annual flood has finally arrived, bringing new prey and new challenges for the big cats. Gordon Buchanan follows the hungry lion mothers as they hunt buffalo, whilst the eldest lion cub, Mathata, learns to avoid this formidable prey. Anna Dimitriadis tracks Mushi, a skinny young cheetah struggling to catch food in the changing landscape. Brad Bestelink is sure Xudum the leopard is pregnant and looking for a den, but rising flood waters are pushing dangerous male leopards into her territory.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: A second visit to Royal Holloway in Surrey where Michael Aspel and the experts discover a belt clasp linking Annie Oakley and Queen Victoria, a ring with an unusual coloured diamond, two bargain jugs and a 'very rare' gold watch - not to mention the collection of dog collars, the box of wax doll's limbs and the Japanese rats.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The Flog It! team get frightened as Paul Martin heads to the spooky Dartmoor landscape, and Caroline Hawley and Mark Stacey find strange things occurring in the queue. Paul Martin discovers a piece of music history with a platinum disc signed by the boys of Coldplay, and we talk to an expert in America about a walking stick associated with General Tom Thumb.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Deirdre O'Kane, Jay Rayner, Tessa Sanderson and Iwan Thomas take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo embarks on a thrilling new railway adventure following the Silk Road through the most populous country of Central Asia, Uzbekistan. At the meeting point of east and west, this region has been home to some of the world’s greatest empires: ruled by the Mongols, the ferocious conqueror Tamerlane, imperial Russia and the Soviet Union. Michael begins in the capital, Tashkent, where he takes in its vast, vibrant market and samples popular Uzbek delicacies. He travels on the lavishly decorated Soviet-era metro, which was hidden from the outside world until 2018, when a ban on photographing it was lifted. Michael hears how an earthquake resulted in Tashkent becoming the capital of Soviet modernist architecture, and he makes his TikTok debut with a globally famous Uzbek social media star.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Andrew and dad Terrence are spinning plates on the farm, and with their glamping pods, just as the latest member of the Glenn family arrives. Long days on the dairy shed build and an infection in Adam’s leg mean he is desperate for a new prosthetic. Meanwhile, Ally and fellow crofters set sail to the stunning volcanic Shiant Isles, where they must navigate steep cliffs to find and shear sheep.

programme.title: The Elon Musk Show
programme.desc: In 2009, the financial crash sends shockwaves across the world and threatens to cripple Elon. To realise his dream, Elon must gain the confidence of the financial markets to allow his electric car company Tesla to become viable. Elon’s space rocket enterprise, SpaceX, is awarded a Nasa contract and starts to enjoy success. However, Tesla is on the ropes and haemorrhaging money. To compound this pressure, Elon is about to marry his second wife, British actress Talulah Riley. Despite these challenges, Elon is determined to create a new car, the Model S, that he believes will be the first mass-produced all-electric car in history.

programme.title: Children of the Blitz
programme.desc: From September 1940 to May 1941, during the Second World War, over 35,000 tonnes of bombs and incendiaries were dropped on towns and cities across the UK during the infamous Luftwaffe aerial bombing campaign that became known as the Blitz. Just before the outbreak of war, the British government’s Operation Pied Piper put plans in place to evacuate millions of children, but only 800,000 left towns and cities that were vulnerable to attack. These are the stories of some of the two million children who stayed at home, often to help their families or because their parents couldn’t bear to send them away. This documentary features some of the last people who witnessed the reality of the Blitz, with their testimony offering an intimate, enlightening and moving portrait of wartime Britain through children’s eyes.

Just before the outbreak of war, the British government’s Operation Pied Piper put plans in place to evacuate millions of children, but only 800,000 left towns and cities that were vulnerable to attack. These are the stories of some of the two million children who stayed at home, often to help their families or because their parents couldn’t bear to send them away. This documentary features some of the last people who witnessed the reality of the Blitz, with their testimony offering an intimate, enlightening and moving portrait of wartime Britain through children’s eyes.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay hosts this quiz celebrating the UK and all its quirks. Alongside him, Traitors star Paul Gorton acts as an unreliable guide, leading a daily tour packed with fun, facts and fibs. This week’s celebrity contestants are TV icon Anneka Rice, comedian Shane Todd and Radio 1Xtra DJ Remi Burgz. The week kicks off in Whitby, with a daily winner and scores building up to eventually reveal a weekly champion.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the final leg of his journey, Michael travels to South Korea’s south west, where food, protest and landscape reveal the values that have shaped the modern nation. Arriving by high-speed train in Gwangju, he explores the region’s deep-rooted food culture, meeting a prizewinning kimchi maker to learn how Korea’s iconic fermented dish has sustained communities for centuries and become a symbol of shared labour and tradition. Michael then confronts a darker chapter in South Korea’s history at the May 18th Memorial Park, where a survivor of the 1980 Gwangju Uprising recounts how student-led protests against military rule were brutally suppressed and why the events are now regarded as the cornerstone of Korean democracy. Leaving the mainland, Michael crosses by ferry to Jeju Island, a volcanic landscape dominated by Mount Halla. Exploring lava tubes with a volcanologist, he uncovers how the island was formed before meeting the Haenyeo, Jeju’s legendary female free divers.

programme.title: Secret Garden
programme.desc: David Attenborough reveals how a remote garden on Scotland’s west coast has become an oasis for barn owls and pine martens as they battle the elements to feed, breed and survive.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Kelly Cates presents highlights from the day’s four Premier League games including West Ham against Arsenal, a game that could have huge implications at the bottom of the table and in the title race. With European places at stake, Aston Villa travel to relegated Burnley, and Everton are at Crystal Palace, while Nottingham Forest look to move clear of the relegation zone at home to Newcastle.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Celebrating the programme's 50th year, Clive Myrie presents the first heat of this series of the classic quiz where contenders face the famous black chair with the ultimate goal of becoming the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are Francisco de Goya, Peaky Blinders, Team GB at the 2020 Summer Olympics and the Philip Marlowe novels of Raymond Chandler.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions while our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The Clean It Fix It team is in West London to help the Parkinson family. With four young children, their house is overrun with toys, the hallway is a dumping ground, and the kitchen is in desperate need of a clean. The team has just one day to transform the space into a clean and clutter-free family home.

programme.title: Big Cats 24/7
programme.desc: The annual flood has finally arrived, bringing new prey and new challenges for the big cats. Gordon Buchanan follows the hungry lion mothers as they hunt buffalo, whilst the eldest lion cub, Mathata, learns to avoid this formidable prey. Anna Dimitriadis tracks Mushi, a skinny young cheetah struggling to catch food in the changing landscape. Brad Bestelink is sure Xudum the leopard is pregnant and looking for a den, but rising flood waters are pushing dangerous male leopards into her territory.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: A second visit to Royal Holloway in Surrey where Michael Aspel and the experts discover a belt clasp linking Annie Oakley and Queen Victoria, a ring with an unusual coloured diamond, two bargain jugs and a 'very rare' gold watch - not to mention the collection of dog collars, the box of wax doll's limbs and the Japanese rats.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The Flog It! team get frightened as Paul Martin heads to the spooky Dartmoor landscape, and Caroline Hawley and Mark Stacey find strange things occurring in the queue. Paul Martin discovers a piece of music history with a platinum disc signed by the boys of Coldplay, and we talk to an expert in America about a walking stick associated with General Tom Thumb.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Deirdre O'Kane, Jay Rayner, Tessa Sanderson and Iwan Thomas take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo embarks on a thrilling new railway adventure following the Silk Road through the most populous country of Central Asia, Uzbekistan. At the meeting point of east and west, this region has been home to some of the world’s greatest empires: ruled by the Mongols, the ferocious conqueror Tamerlane, imperial Russia and the Soviet Union. Michael begins in the capital, Tashkent, where he takes in its vast, vibrant market and samples popular Uzbek delicacies. He travels on the lavishly decorated Soviet-era metro, which was hidden from the outside world until 2018, when a ban on photographing it was lifted. Michael hears how an earthquake resulted in Tashkent becoming the capital of Soviet modernist architecture, and he makes his TikTok debut with a globally famous Uzbek social media star.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Andrew and dad Terrence are spinning plates on the farm, and with their glamping pods, just as the latest member of the Glenn family arrives. Long days on the dairy shed build and an infection in Adam’s leg mean he is desperate for a new prosthetic. Meanwhile, Ally and fellow crofters set sail to the stunning volcanic Shiant Isles, where they must navigate steep cliffs to find and shear sheep.

programme.title: The Elon Musk Show
programme.desc: In 2009, the financial crash sends shockwaves across the world and threatens to cripple Elon. To realise his dream, Elon must gain the confidence of the financial markets to allow his electric car company Tesla to become viable. Elon’s space rocket enterprise, SpaceX, is awarded a Nasa contract and starts to enjoy success. However, Tesla is on the ropes and haemorrhaging money. To compound this pressure, Elon is about to marry his second wife, British actress Talulah Riley. Despite these challenges, Elon is determined to create a new car, the Model S, that he believes will be the first mass-produced all-electric car in history.

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: After nearly five thousand miles, the Hairy Bikers reach the last leg of their Bakeation which takes them through northern Spain. Their journey starts in San Sebastian, where they get stuck in to the local cuisine with pinchos - tapas gone large! They also learn the secret properties of spelt, Europe's forgotten grain, and use it to bake not only bread, but a giant spelt sausage roll, packed with chorizo. Their 5,000-mile adventure ends in Santiago de Compostela with a spectacular firework display to celebrate the 800th anniversary of St James. Great food and great company, the Spanish leg is a fitting end to the Hairy Bikers brilliant Bakeation.

programme.title: Operation Ouch!
programme.desc: To investigate why tummy rumbles are so loud when you’re hungry, the doctors call in the supersized stomach of Mega Xand! When Dr Chris and Dr Xand count down the Top 5 Bizarre-est Body Parts You Never Knew You Had, you will discover that the mysterious palmaris longus is so bizarre that you might not have it at all! The big question in Ouchology is whether it will be Dr Chris, Dr Xand or Dr Ronx who gets snotted by their kid quizmasters. If the doctors can put all the organs in the right place on their own bodies, they could win enough points to avoid the snot - but someone has to come last! Elsewhere, for Investigation Ouch!, Dr Chris finds out why real doctors are doing fake operations on fake organs inside fake patients in Nottingham. At the emergency department in Edinburgh, Alice has hurt her head and arm by accidentally running into a fence. And when Finlay arrives with burns on his forearms, the medics think it might have something to do with parsnips!

programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a bedroom, where they watch a young man going to sleep under a knitted blanket. The Twirlywoos see a loose bit of wool from the end of the blanket get caught on the foot of the bed, and as the man pulls the blanket up over himself it starts to unravel. The Twirlywoos are fascinated by this and they start to pull the loose bit of wool, making the blanket shorter and shorter, while the man remains obliviously asleep. They fly away when the hooter sounds and the man wakes up to find he only has a thin strip of blanket left! Undeterred, he ties it around his neck like a scarf and goes back to sleep. The Very Important Lady visits the boat, and falls apart. Some of the sections of her body roll away, so that when the Twirlywoos put her back together she is too short. Each time the lady collapses in frustration another section rolls away, making her even shorter when the Twirlywoos put her together again! The missing parts of the lady are blocking Peekaboo's door, so he boots them out, and the Twirlywoos finally build her up to the correct height.

Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are Sticks which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding safe, baby appropriate sticks inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun rhyme ‘One, Two, Buckle My Shoe’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.desc: When the Squirrels search for Enid, they are surprised to hear her meow from the top of the Mighty Sugar Bun Mountain. The Squirrels prepare for the climb to rescue Enid, but first Duggee teaches them what they need to pack in their backpacks for a successful trip. The team walk through rocky terrain, grey skies, plentiful rain and snow blizzards but keep morale high as they learn how phrasing negative thoughts into helpful ones will let them overcome any challenges along the way. The Squirrels repeat their positive affirmations to keep climbing up the Sugar Bun as a team, and when they find themselves at the top of the mountain, they all give Enid a big hug. A successful rescue mission means Happy can have his nap on the sofa with Enid when they are back!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Ladybird sings about all his favourite animals. He really loves them all.

programme.desc: Kyra and Khloe plan a visit to Nana and make chocolate crispy cakes to surprise her with. But will Nana enjoy the cakes? And will the worm be alright?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Aniyah is cooking a Brazilian national dish for us today: feijoada, a stew containing black beans and lots of other delicious ingredients, which is served with rice. Aniyah works hard to prepare all the ingredients, including squeezing her own fresh orange juice and tearing up cabbage leaves to go on top. Brazil is famous for its carnivals, so Aniyah's table is carnival-themed, complete with bright, colourful headdresses for her friends to wear while they eat.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today's episode, Maddie finds out about things that use water. She visits an aquatic centre to show us how a fish tank works, using a special underwater camera to explain how a filter works inside a tank to help keep the water clean and free from fish waste. Next, Maddie visits a factory to find out how bath tubs are made. Starting with a thin sheet of plastic, she shows us how the bath is moulded by air suction. She uses a special camera to explain how a fibreglass gun is used to make the bath strong enough for us to use.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Dan the Border collie is a search and rescue dog who works with his owner Jamie. His super nose follows scents and smells like clues so they can rescue people who need their help. Dan and Jamie have been called to the care home by police officer Penny because an elderly gentleman has gone missing. His name is Robert, but he likes to be called Pop-Pop. He only moved into the care home recently and loves to explore, but he sometimes loses his way Dan is a mountain dog who loves an urban rescue. There are lots of new scents for his super nose to explore. Since Pop-Pop loves flowers, Dan and Jamie straight head to the flower shop, where Flora the florist recognises Pop-Pop’s photo. He stopped by earlier to buy some tulips and was carrying a bag of bird seed. Following the mysterious trail of clues, Jamie and Dan head to the park to track Pop-Pop down. Can they find him in time for supper?

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet some painted dogs. They notice the wild dogs' splattered yellow and brown coats, which is where they get their name from. Their coloured coats help camouflage or hide them when they're hunting on the African plains. Next, Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet some coatis. Close relatives of the racoon, these nimble creatures have lovely black-and-white ringed tails, and they use their long, bendy noses to find food hidden in the ground. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: Bing

It looks as though Sula will have to hop home, until Bing finds a way to turn the 'bad-bye' back into a goodbye again.

We see lots of different presents - a wrapped-up present, one with a bow, another for a birthday and a present to make you feel better. There are some for parties, one made by a squirrel and another that is just because! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
