programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a bedroom, where they watch a young man going to sleep under a knitted blanket. The Twirlywoos see a loose bit of wool from the end of the blanket get caught on the foot of the bed, and as the man pulls the blanket up over himself it starts to unravel. The Twirlywoos are fascinated by this and they start to pull the loose bit of wool, making the blanket shorter and shorter, while the man remains obliviously asleep. They fly away when the hooter sounds and the man wakes up to find he only has a thin strip of blanket left! Undeterred, he ties it around his neck like a scarf and goes back to sleep. The Very Important Lady visits the boat, and falls apart. Some of the sections of her body roll away, so that when the Twirlywoos put her back together she is too short. Each time the lady collapses in frustration another section rolls away, making her even shorter when the Twirlywoos put her together again! The missing parts of the lady are blocking Peekaboo's door, so he boots them out, and the Twirlywoos finally build her up to the correct height.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Mr Tumble gets in a muddle while helping Grandad Tumble look after the garden. Justin meets Ryan, his new friend, in a walled garden to help take care of the plants. George joins them to do some watering. There's a decorative recycling spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words seeds, garden and plant.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky and Dipsy both want a go with Tinky Winky's bag and start to squabble. The Noo-noo sucks up the bag and only gives it back when Tinky Winky and Dipsy are ready to share.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Layla, Betsy, Tobias, Amelia, Amber, Ferne, Ezra and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are Sticks which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding safe, baby appropriate sticks inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun rhyme ‘One, Two, Buckle My Shoe’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children create animal masks to pretend to be farm animals, learn signs for farm, old and pig, and sing and sign Old MacDonald Had a Farm.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Aaron, Novah and Joda go on a springtime adventure, meeting a beatboxing daffodil to find out why all the plants are starting to wake up.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: It’s recycling day in the attic – and it's also Murphi’s hairdo day! The first idea is a hilarious hairdo pot, the Mini Monsters make a variety of cheese box octopuses, and the Magic Monster Mirror brings a call from Rebecca’s aunt. Finally, the Recycling Express arrives with some buttons that Murphi and Rebecca use to create a brilliant box robot.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger can't get a wink of sleep when the baby Pea-Rexes start snoring loudly.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: When Bluey forgets to put her favourite toy away, cousin Socks grabs it and won’t let go! The kids stage a horsey wedding to distract her, with Dad and Uncle Stripe as the horses!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: When the Squirrels search for Enid, they are surprised to hear her meow from the top of the Mighty Sugar Bun Mountain. The Squirrels prepare for the climb to rescue Enid, but first Duggee teaches them what they need to pack in their backpacks for a successful trip. The team walk through rocky terrain, grey skies, plentiful rain and snow blizzards but keep morale high as they learn how phrasing negative thoughts into helpful ones will let them overcome any challenges along the way. The Squirrels repeat their positive affirmations to keep climbing up the Sugar Bun as a team, and when they find themselves at the top of the mountain, they all give Enid a big hug. A successful rescue mission means Happy can have his nap on the sofa with Enid when they are back!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Ladybird sings about all his favourite animals. He really loves them all.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk to a bridge to play Billy Goat’s Gruff. On the way, they tip-toe across lava, blow down a straw house, walk like robots and even stroke a Chinese stone lion!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Kyra and Khloe plan a visit to Nana and make chocolate crispy cakes to surprise her with. Visiting Nana is a special occasion, so Mum draws pretty patterns on Kyra and Khloe’s hands using henna. At Nana’s they have a delicious picnic in the garden and then rescue a worm! But will Nana enjoy the cakes? And will the worm be alright?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Aniyah is cooking a Brazilian national dish for us today: feijoada, a stew containing black beans and lots of other delicious ingredients, which is served with rice. Aniyah works hard to prepare all the ingredients, including squeezing her own fresh orange juice and tearing up cabbage leaves to go on top. Brazil is famous for its carnivals, so Aniyah's table is carnival-themed, complete with bright, colourful headdresses for her friends to wear while they eat.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today's episode, Maddie finds out about things that use water. She visits an aquatic centre to show us how a fish tank works, using a special underwater camera to explain how a filter works inside a tank to help keep the water clean and free from fish waste. Next, Maddie visits a factory to find out how bath tubs are made. Starting with a thin sheet of plastic, she shows us how the bath is moulded by air suction. She uses a special camera to explain how a fibreglass gun is used to make the bath strong enough for us to use.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Dan the Border collie is a search and rescue dog who works with his owner Jamie. His super nose follows scents and smells like clues so they can rescue people who need their help. Dan and Jamie have been called to the care home by police officer Penny because an elderly gentleman has gone missing. His name is Robert, but he likes to be called Pop-Pop. He only moved into the care home recently and loves to explore, but he sometimes loses his way Dan is a mountain dog who loves an urban rescue. There are lots of new scents for his super nose to explore. Since Pop-Pop loves flowers, Dan and Jamie straight head to the flower shop, where Flora the florist recognises Pop-Pop’s photo. He stopped by earlier to buy some tulips and was carrying a bag of bird seed. Following the mysterious trail of clues, Jamie and Dan head to the park to track Pop-Pop down. Can they find him in time for supper?

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet some painted dogs. They notice the wild dogs' splattered yellow and brown coats, which is where they get their name from. Their coloured coats help camouflage or hide them when they're hunting on the African plains. Next, Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet some coatis. Close relatives of the racoon, these nimble creatures have lovely black-and-white ringed tails, and they use their long, bendy noses to find food hidden in the ground. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is sad that Mrs Hobbs and her cat, George, are soon to leave Maple Close. The Brooklyn-Bells call on Mrs Hobbs to persuade her not to move house, only to find that her cat, George, has fleas. They offer to help and discover a secret about Mrs Hobbs.

programme.title: How To Clean Up For Cash
programme.desc: Josie and the gang head to Glasgow to assist Caitlan in clearing out her grandmother Susan's lifetime of car boot finds. Over the years, Susan and her husband Dennis amassed countless items from car boot sales but since his passing three years ago, Susan's been left with a home full of belongings which has become overwhelming. Josie and the team face their most sensitive project to date as they have to secretly help Susan let go emotionally and physically, while respecting Dennis's memory. Josie discovers that Caitlan is a clutter culprit too, and as she was raised by Susan and Dennis since she was a baby, she also has an emotional connection to the clutter. Jacqui equips Caitlan with the tools to de-clutter, whilst Dan unearths some hidden treasures - from a Waltham skeleton watch to 22 carat rings. After shopping in Perth on the fake show, Susan returns home to discover her car boot finds all boxed up and valued. Is she ready to part with a lifetime of belongings and take the cash?

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2007, student Carrie Symonds is picked up by Worboys, hears his story of a 'casino win', and reluctantly drinks a drugged glass of vodka. She wakes up distressed, but is certain that she wasn't assaulted, and thinks little more of it. Meanwhile, Sarah struggles with the psychological impact of her attack, straining her relationship with Jack's father and hindering her attempts at new relationships. Another student, Laila, becomes separated from friends on a night out and encounters Worboys. She is also drugged and assaulted, before being dumped outside her accommodation. She endures the same humiliating process as Sarah, including, she says, being asked if she's the 'kind of girl that wears red nail varnish'. CCTV footage of Worboys' cab is secured, but despite being brought in for questioning, he's released without charge. Months later, Laila's case is also dropped. Soon after that, Worboys strikes again, but this time a routine police sweep flags the case and a driver is arrested.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Set in the heart of The Peak District, six households from across the UK move into a 'picture-perfect' village to compete for a massive £250,000 prize. It's the penultimate day on Keep Your Enemies Close as the neighbours focus on the true nature of their relationships and who they can really trust. The pressure is on - one wrong move and they could be gone! Graham hosts an exclusive supper with a cruel twist: only three of the four remaining households will receive an invitation. The neighbours must compete against the clock in a series of parlour games, and the winner is guaranteed a place at the table - for everyone else, their fate hinges entirely on their popularity. Who has managed to secure enough public favour to make it to the final?

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's JB Gill, Nish Kumar, Lindsey Santoro and Aurie Styla joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

Josie and the team face their most sensitive project to date as they have to secretly help Susan let go emotionally and physically, while respecting Dennis's memory. Josie discovers that Caitlan is a clutter culprit too, and as she was raised by Susan and Dennis since she was a baby, she also has an emotional connection to the clutter. Jacqui equips Caitlan with the tools to de-clutter, whilst Dan unearths some hidden treasures - from a Waltham skeleton watch to 22 carat rings. After shopping in Perth on the fake show, Susan returns home to discover her car boot finds all boxed up and valued. Is she ready to part with a lifetime of belongings and take the cash?

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2007, student Carrie Symonds is picked up by Worboys, hears his story of a 'casino win', and reluctantly drinks a drugged glass of vodka. She wakes up distressed, but is certain that she wasn't assaulted, and thinks little more of it. Meanwhile, Sarah struggles with the psychological impact of her attack, straining her relationship with Jack's father and hindering her attempts at new relationships. Another student, Laila, becomes separated from friends on a night out and encounters Worboys. She is also drugged and assaulted, before being dumped outside her accommodation. She endures the same humiliating process as Sarah, including, she says, being asked if she's the 'kind of girl that wears red nail varnish'. CCTV footage of Worboys' cab is secured, but despite being brought in for questioning, he's released without charge. Months later, Laila's case is also dropped. Soon after that, Worboys strikes again, but this time a routine police sweep flags the case and a driver is arrested.

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's JB Gill, Nish Kumar, Lindsey Santoro and Aurie Styla joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.title: How To Clean Up For Cash
programme.desc: Josie and the gang head to Glasgow to assist Caitlan in clearing out her grandmother Susan's lifetime of car boot finds. Over the years, Susan and her husband Dennis amassed countless items from car boot sales but since his passing three years ago, Susan's been left with a home full of belongings which has become overwhelming. Josie and the team face their most sensitive project to date as they have to secretly help Susan let go emotionally and physically, while respecting Dennis's memory. Josie discovers that Caitlan is a clutter culprit too, and as she was raised by Susan and Dennis since she was a baby, she also has an emotional connection to the clutter. Jacqui equips Caitlan with the tools to de-clutter, whilst Dan unearths some hidden treasures - from a Waltham skeleton watch to 22 carat rings. After shopping in Perth on the fake show, Susan returns home to discover her car boot finds all boxed up and valued. Is she ready to part with a lifetime of belongings and take the cash?

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2007, student Carrie Symonds is picked up by Worboys, hears his story of a 'casino win', and reluctantly drinks a drugged glass of vodka. She wakes up distressed, but is certain that she wasn't assaulted, and thinks little more of it. Meanwhile, Sarah struggles with the psychological impact of her attack, straining her relationship with Jack's father and hindering her attempts at new relationships. Another student, Laila, becomes separated from friends on a night out and encounters Worboys. She is also drugged and assaulted, before being dumped outside her accommodation. She endures the same humiliating process as Sarah, including, she says, being asked if she's the 'kind of girl that wears red nail varnish'. CCTV footage of Worboys' cab is secured, but despite being brought in for questioning, he's released without charge. Months later, Laila's case is also dropped. Soon after that, Worboys strikes again, but this time a routine police sweep flags the case and a driver is arrested.

Set in the heart of The Peak District, six households from across the UK move into a 'picture-perfect' village to compete for a massive £250,000 prize. Who has managed to secure enough public favour to make it to the final?

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's JB Gill, Nish Kumar, Lindsey Santoro and Aurie Styla joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

She wakes up distressed, but is certain that she wasn't assaulted, and thinks little more of it. Meanwhile, Sarah struggles with the psychological impact of her attack, straining her relationship with Jack's father and hindering her attempts at new relationships. Another student, Laila, becomes separated from friends on a night out and encounters Worboys. She is also drugged and assaulted, before being dumped outside her accommodation. She endures the same humiliating process as Sarah, including, she says, being asked if she's the 'kind of girl that wears red nail varnish'. CCTV footage of Worboys' cab is secured, but despite being brought in for questioning, he's released without charge. Months later, Laila's case is also dropped. Soon after that, Worboys strikes again, but this time a routine police sweep flags the case and a driver is arrested.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Set in the heart of The Peak District, six households from across the UK move into a 'picture-perfect' village to compete for a massive £250,000 prize. It's the penultimate day on Keep Your Enemies Close as the neighbours focus on the true nature of their relationships and who they can really trust. The pressure is on - one wrong move and they could be gone! Graham hosts an exclusive supper with a cruel twist: only three of the four remaining households will receive an invitation. The neighbours must compete against the clock in a series of parlour games, and the winner is guaranteed a place at the table - for everyone else, their fate hinges entirely on their popularity. Who has managed to secure enough public favour to make it to the final?

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's JB Gill, Nish Kumar, Lindsey Santoro and Aurie Styla joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.title: How To Clean Up For Cash
programme.desc: Josie and the gang head to Glasgow to assist Caitlan in clearing out her grandmother Susan's lifetime of car boot finds. Over the years, Susan and her husband Dennis amassed countless items from car boot sales but since his passing three years ago, Susan's been left with a home full of belongings which has become overwhelming. Josie and the team face their most sensitive project to date as they have to secretly help Susan let go emotionally and physically, while respecting Dennis's memory. Josie discovers that Caitlan is a clutter culprit too, and as she was raised by Susan and Dennis since she was a baby, she also has an emotional connection to the clutter. Jacqui equips Caitlan with the tools to de-clutter, whilst Dan unearths some hidden treasures - from a Waltham skeleton watch to 22 carat rings. After shopping in Perth on the fake show, Susan returns home to discover her car boot finds all boxed up and valued. Is she ready to part with a lifetime of belongings and take the cash?

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2007, student Carrie Symonds is picked up by Worboys, hears his story of a 'casino win', and reluctantly drinks a drugged glass of vodka. She wakes up distressed, but is certain that she wasn't assaulted, and thinks little more of it. Meanwhile, Sarah struggles with the psychological impact of her attack, straining her relationship with Jack's father and hindering her attempts at new relationships. Another student, Laila, becomes separated from friends on a night out and encounters Worboys. She is also drugged and assaulted, before being dumped outside her accommodation. She endures the same humiliating process as Sarah, including, she says, being asked if she's the 'kind of girl that wears red nail varnish'. CCTV footage of Worboys' cab is secured, but despite being brought in for questioning, he's released without charge. Months later, Laila's case is also dropped. Soon after that, Worboys strikes again, but this time a routine police sweep flags the case and a driver is arrested.

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's JB Gill, Nish Kumar, Lindsey Santoro and Aurie Styla joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.desc: Josie and the gang head to Glasgow to assist Caitlan in clearing out her grandmother Susan's lifetime of car boot finds. After shopping in Perth on the fake show, Susan returns home to discover her car boot finds all boxed up and valued. Is she ready to part with a lifetime of belongings and take the cash?

programme.title: How To Clean Up For Cash
programme.desc: Josie and the gang head to Glasgow to assist Caitlan in clearing out her grandmother Susan's lifetime of car boot finds. Over the years, Susan and her husband Dennis amassed countless items from car boot sales but since his passing three years ago, Susan's been left with a home full of belongings which has become overwhelming. Josie and the team face their most sensitive project to date as they have to secretly help Susan let go emotionally and physically, while respecting Dennis's memory. Josie discovers that Caitlan is a clutter culprit too, and as she was raised by Susan and Dennis since she was a baby, she also has an emotional connection to the clutter. Jacqui equips Caitlan with the tools to de-clutter, whilst Dan unearths some hidden treasures - from a Waltham skeleton watch to 22 carat rings. After shopping in Perth on the fake show, Susan returns home to discover her car boot finds all boxed up and valued. Is she ready to part with a lifetime of belongings and take the cash?

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2007, student Carrie Symonds is picked up by Worboys, hears his story of a 'casino win', and reluctantly drinks a drugged glass of vodka. She wakes up distressed, but is certain that she wasn't assaulted, and thinks little more of it. Meanwhile, Sarah struggles with the psychological impact of her attack, straining her relationship with Jack's father and hindering her attempts at new relationships. Another student, Laila, becomes separated from friends on a night out and encounters Worboys. She is also drugged and assaulted, before being dumped outside her accommodation. She endures the same humiliating process as Sarah, including, she says, being asked if she's the 'kind of girl that wears red nail varnish'. CCTV footage of Worboys' cab is secured, but despite being brought in for questioning, he's released without charge. Months later, Laila's case is also dropped. Soon after that, Worboys strikes again, but this time a routine police sweep flags the case and a driver is arrested.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Set in the heart of The Peak District, six households from across the UK move into a 'picture-perfect' village to compete for a massive £250,000 prize. It's the penultimate day on Keep Your Enemies Close as the neighbours focus on the true nature of their relationships and who they can really trust. The pressure is on - one wrong move and they could be gone! Graham hosts an exclusive supper with a cruel twist: only three of the four remaining households will receive an invitation. The neighbours must compete against the clock in a series of parlour games, and the winner is guaranteed a place at the table - for everyone else, their fate hinges entirely on their popularity. Who has managed to secure enough public favour to make it to the final?

Set in the heart of The Peak District, six households from across the UK move into a 'picture-perfect' village to compete for a massive £250,000 prize. It's the penultimate day on Keep Your Enemies Close as the neighbours focus on the true nature of their relationships and who they can really trust. The pressure is on - one wrong move and they could be gone! Graham hosts an exclusive supper with a cruel twist: only three of the four remaining households will receive an invitation. The neighbours must compete against the clock in a series of parlour games, and the winner is guaranteed a place at the table - for everyone else, their fate hinges entirely on their popularity. Who has managed to secure enough public favour to make it to the final?

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's JB Gill, Nish Kumar, Lindsey Santoro and Aurie Styla joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.title: How To Clean Up For Cash
programme.desc: Josie and the gang head to Glasgow to assist Caitlan in clearing out her grandmother Susan's lifetime of car boot finds. Over the years, Susan and her husband Dennis amassed countless items from car boot sales but since his passing three years ago, Susan's been left with a home full of belongings which has become overwhelming. Josie and the team face their most sensitive project to date as they have to secretly help Susan let go emotionally and physically, while respecting Dennis's memory. Josie discovers that Caitlan is a clutter culprit too, and as she was raised by Susan and Dennis since she was a baby, she also has an emotional connection to the clutter. Jacqui equips Caitlan with the tools to de-clutter, whilst Dan unearths some hidden treasures - from a Waltham skeleton watch to 22 carat rings. After shopping in Perth on the fake show, Susan returns home to discover her car boot finds all boxed up and valued. Is she ready to part with a lifetime of belongings and take the cash?

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2007, student Carrie Symonds is picked up by Worboys, hears his story of a 'casino win', and reluctantly drinks a drugged glass of vodka. She wakes up distressed, but is certain that she wasn't assaulted, and thinks little more of it. Meanwhile, Sarah struggles with the psychological impact of her attack, straining her relationship with Jack's father and hindering her attempts at new relationships. Another student, Laila, becomes separated from friends on a night out and encounters Worboys. She is also drugged and assaulted, before being dumped outside her accommodation. She endures the same humiliating process as Sarah, including, she says, being asked if she's the 'kind of girl that wears red nail varnish'. CCTV footage of Worboys' cab is secured, but despite being brought in for questioning, he's released without charge. Months later, Laila's case is also dropped. Soon after that, Worboys strikes again, but this time a routine police sweep flags the case and a driver is arrested.

programme.desc: Comedy series providing an honest, uplifting and heart-warming portrayal of the lives of working-class teenagers from Liverpool while tackling issues with a refreshing humour. It's Diversity and Inclusion Week and The Brimble, the most 'woke' girl at the school, has convinced the headmaster that the pupils should be set the task of pairing up with their polar opposite and present their differences and common ground in a presentation. Mo, who has fancied The Brimble for ages, spots his opportunity to try and impress her by suggesting they team up as he is a devout practising Muslim (he's not). Fascinated by his alleged faith, The Brimble leaps at the chance and asks if she can come to his house to observe a real Muslim family - keen to keep up the pretence, Mo calls his non-practicing Muslim parents and begs them to help him out. They agree... but when Mo and The Brimble arrive at the house, it becomes apparent that they are going to teach their son a life lesson about truth and faith.

Locals blame the 'beast of Midsomer', but Barnaby is unconvinced, especially when he discovers that umpire and retired spymaster Malcolm Frazer is using his home, Allenby House, as a safe house. Soon Barnaby discovers links to a spy ring that operated in Berlin during the Cold War, but his investigation is obstructed at every turn, and it seems as though shady dealings are still going on at Allenby House. programme.title: The Roof
programme.desc: 1933. Inspector Darrow (Leslie Perrins) investigates the death of a wealthy man (George Zucco). [S]

programme.title: Cinebox Memories
programme.desc: Enjoy English beat band Freddie and the Dreamers as they perform the fantastic hit You Were Made For Me.

programme.title: The Rogues
programme.desc: The Real Russian Caviar. 1965. Gig Young, David Niven and Charles Boyer are The Rogues, members of two related families of international forgers and conmen. [S]

programme.title: The Adventures of Robin Hood
programme.desc: Errand of Mercy. 1956. Stars Richard Greene, Victor Woolf & Rufus Cruickshank. A herbalist looking for remedies to help the sick as Robin passes by but dies before he can complete the mission. [S]

programme.title: The Buccaneers
programme.desc: Blood Will Tell. 1957. Stars Robert Shaw, Dawson France & John Dearth. The trader's estate, Gresham Island, is in jeopardy. A lawyer arrives at the colony in search of the last remaining heir. [S]

programme.title: William Tell
programme.desc: Landslide. 1959. Stars: Conrad Phillips, Willoughby Goddard & Jennifer Jayne. Tell comes face to face with his exact double - an Austrian imported by Gessler to impersonate the resistance leader. [S]

programme.title: The Vise
programme.desc: Set a Murderer. 1954. Stars Honor Blackman, Martin Boddey, Clifford Evans. Two successful businessmen have a monopoly of the market in their particular field but suddenly a new competitor arrives. [S]

programme.title: The Large Rope
programme.desc: (AKA: The Long Rope). 1953. Drama. Director: Wolf Rilla. Stars Donald Houston, Susan Shaw & Peter Byrne. A man returns to where he was accused of murdering a girl to prove his innocence. [S]

programme.title: Ferranti Masters of Power 1935
programme.desc: 1935. An informative short film about the intricate power systems that help to supply the many radio stations that can be received.

programme.title: Glencannon: A Nosegay...
programme.desc: ...for Mr Montgomery. 1957. Comedy. Stars Thomas Mitchell & Patrick Allen. There is a bonus for the crew member who improves public relations the most. Glencannon has an outlandish scheme. [S]

programme.title: Take a Letter Mr Jones
programme.desc: Business Before Pleasure. 1981. Starring John Inman & Rula Lenska. One of the chief executives has arrived from America and it puts the office, particularly Joan, in a flap. [S]

programme.title: Park Ranger
programme.desc: 1978. Waste. Featuring Norman Bowler as a trainee warden in a national park. [S] (S1, E05)

programme.title: Look At Life Running Dry
programme.desc: 1964. A Look at drought of 1959 and the question of whether Britain's water supplies are organised efficiently.

programme.title: Live It Up
programme.desc: 1963. Featuring music from the likes of Kenny Ball, Gene Vincent and Heinz. A pop film classic from the golden era. Dave (David Hemmings) and his mates are GPO riders who dream of becoming stars. [S]

programme.title: Radio Caroline 1965
programme.desc: A fascinating short film about the radio ship broadcasting from the North Sea, Radio Caroline. Learn about the station from its beginning in 1964!

programme.title: Star Performance
programme.desc: The Rites of Spring. 1956. Comedy. Director Roy Kellino. Stars David Niven, Ernest Anderson & Lela Bliss. A husband sends his young wife flowers from a 'secret admirer' as a test of her fidelity. [S]

programme.title: Look At Life Chicken In The Mill
programme.desc: 1961. A look into the new industrial revolution in Lancashire; from 1950, more than 55 cotton mills were converted for light industries. This film examines the change for Lancashire's workers.

programme.title: Sergeant Cork
programme.desc: The Case of the Respectable Suicide. 1963. Stars John Barrie, William Gaunt & June Watts. A wealthy man takes his life, his will states that his money is left to his housekeeper not his wife. [S]

programme.title: Richard the Lionheart
programme.desc: The King's Champion. 1962. Stars Dermot Walsh, John Bay & Ian Fleming. Led by a pretender to the English throne, a Black Knight issues a challenge that Richard must accept or forfeit his throne. [S]

programme.title: Hell Drivers
programme.desc: 1957. Drama. Director C. Raker Endfield. Stars Stanley Baker, David McCallum, Sid James and Sean Connery. Tom signs up as a 'Hell Driver', but the death-trap roads are the least of his problems. [S]

programme.title: First Comes Courage
programme.desc: 1943. War. Directed by Dorothy Arzner. Stars Merle Oberon, Brian Aherne & Carl Esmond. A member of the Norwegian resistance faces complications when a British commando falls in love with her. [S]

programme.title: The Directors
programme.desc: Alfred Hitchcock defined his own unique style of filmmaking from the early days of the 39 Steps and the Lodger to the Hollywood glamour of North by Northwest. [S]

programme.title: The Veil
programme.desc: Girl on the Road. 1958. Stars Boris Karloff, Tod Andrews & Eve Brent. A traveller stops for a stranded young woman on a lonely road and falls for her but their chance meeting is tied in tragedy. [S]

programme.title: The Footage Detectives
programme.desc: The Detectives take a trip to 1961 with two very different reels, first up is a look at mobile libraries and then they're off to beautiful Scotland. There's also Roy Orbison in Romford! [S]

programme.title: Francis Durbridge's...
programme.desc: ... Bat Out of Hell. 1966. Stars Sylvia Syms, John Thaw & Dudley Foster. A second affair is exposed and it seems that Geoffrey had changed his will leaving his fortunes to someone else. [S]

programme.title: Miracle on 34th Street
programme.desc: 1959. Drama. Director: William Corrigan. Stars Ed Wynn, Peter Lind Hayes & Mary Healy. A kindly old gentleman claims to be the real Santa Claus and has to defend his sanity in court. [S]

programme.title: The Proposition
programme.desc: Drama. Director: John Hillcoat. Stars John Hurt, Guy Pearce & Ray Winstone. A lawman gives an outlaw nine days to kill his older brother, or they'll execute his younger brother. [S]

programme.title: Pearl of the South Pacific
programme.desc: 1955. Adventure. Two beachcombers with a yacht join Rita, a woman with a past, to find black pearls on a secret island. Starring Virginia Mayo and Dennis Morgan.

programme.title: How To Clean Up For Cash
programme.desc: Josie and the gang head to Glasgow to assist Caitlan in clearing out her grandmother Susan's lifetime of car boot finds. Over the years, Susan and her husband Dennis amassed countless items from car boot sales but since his passing three years ago, Susan's been left with a home full of belongings which has become overwhelming. Josie and the team face their most sensitive project to date as they have to secretly help Susan let go emotionally and physically, while respecting Dennis's memory. Josie discovers that Caitlan is a clutter culprit too, and as she was raised by Susan and Dennis since she was a baby, she also has an emotional connection to the clutter. Jacqui equips Caitlan with the tools to de-clutter, whilst Dan unearths some hidden treasures - from a Waltham skeleton watch to 22 carat rings. After shopping in Perth on the fake show, Susan returns home to discover her car boot finds all boxed up and valued. Is she ready to part with a lifetime of belongings and take the cash?

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2007, student Carrie Symonds is picked up by Worboys, hears his story of a 'casino win', and reluctantly drinks a drugged glass of vodka. She wakes up distressed, but is certain that she wasn't assaulted, and thinks little more of it. Meanwhile, Sarah struggles with the psychological impact of her attack, straining her relationship with Jack's father and hindering her attempts at new relationships. Another student, Laila, becomes separated from friends on a night out and encounters Worboys. She is also drugged and assaulted, before being dumped outside her accommodation. She endures the same humiliating process as Sarah, including, she says, being asked if she's the 'kind of girl that wears red nail varnish'. CCTV footage of Worboys' cab is secured, but despite being brought in for questioning, he's released without charge. Months later, Laila's case is also dropped. Soon after that, Worboys strikes again, but this time a routine police sweep flags the case and a driver is arrested.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Set in the heart of The Peak District, six households from across the UK move into a 'picture-perfect' village to compete for a massive £250,000 prize. It's the penultimate day on Keep Your Enemies Close as the neighbours focus on the true nature of their relationships and who they can really trust. The pressure is on - one wrong move and they could be gone! Graham hosts an exclusive supper with a cruel twist: only three of the four remaining households will receive an invitation. The neighbours must compete against the clock in a series of parlour games, and the winner is guaranteed a place at the table - for everyone else, their fate hinges entirely on their popularity. Who has managed to secure enough public favour to make it to the final?

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's JB Gill, Nish Kumar, Lindsey Santoro and Aurie Styla joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.title: How To Clean Up For Cash
programme.desc: Josie and the gang head to Glasgow to assist Caitlan in clearing out her grandmother Susan's lifetime of car boot finds. Over the years, Susan and her husband Dennis amassed countless items from car boot sales but since his passing three years ago, Susan's been left with a home full of belongings which has become overwhelming. Josie and the team face their most sensitive project to date as they have to secretly help Susan let go emotionally and physically, while respecting Dennis's memory. Josie discovers that Caitlan is a clutter culprit too, and as she was raised by Susan and Dennis since she was a baby, she also has an emotional connection to the clutter. Jacqui equips Caitlan with the tools to de-clutter, whilst Dan unearths some hidden treasures - from a Waltham skeleton watch to 22 carat rings. After shopping in Perth on the fake show, Susan returns home to discover her car boot finds all boxed up and valued. Is she ready to part with a lifetime of belongings and take the cash?

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2007, student Carrie Symonds is picked up by Worboys, hears his story of a 'casino win', and reluctantly drinks a drugged glass of vodka. She wakes up distressed, but is certain that she wasn't assaulted, and thinks little more of it. Meanwhile, Sarah struggles with the psychological impact of her attack, straining her relationship with Jack's father and hindering her attempts at new relationships. Another student, Laila, becomes separated from friends on a night out and encounters Worboys. She is also drugged and assaulted, before being dumped outside her accommodation. She endures the same humiliating process as Sarah, including, she says, being asked if she's the 'kind of girl that wears red nail varnish'. CCTV footage of Worboys' cab is secured, but despite being brought in for questioning, he's released without charge. Months later, Laila's case is also dropped. Soon after that, Worboys strikes again, but this time a routine police sweep flags the case and a driver is arrested.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Set in the heart of The Peak District, six households from across the UK move into a 'picture-perfect' village to compete for a massive £250,000 prize. It's the penultimate day on Keep Your Enemies Close as the neighbours focus on the true nature of their relationships and who they can really trust. The pressure is on - one wrong move and they could be gone! Graham hosts an exclusive supper with a cruel twist: only three of the four remaining households will receive an invitation. The neighbours must compete against the clock in a series of parlour games, and the winner is guaranteed a place at the table - for everyone else, their fate hinges entirely on their popularity. Who has managed to secure enough public favour to make it to the final?

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's JB Gill, Nish Kumar, Lindsey Santoro and Aurie Styla joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...
